topics.title: Langflow, Nextcloud, and AhsayCBS Under Live Exploitation
topics.latest_developments: Previdian warned that attackers exploit CVE-2026-105740, a 9.9-rated authenticated remote code execution flaw in Langflow, the open-source AI application builder IBM acquired through DataStax, and logged 1,423 honeypot exploit attempts; three administrators reported on GitHub that attackers plant web shells on Nextcloud servers through the optional Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server app, with the first logged attack on September 10, 2026; and Ahsay Backup of Singapore shipped new fixes for CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 after its earlier patches proved incomplete, a day after CISA put both bugs in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog alongside Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS CVE-2026-0322 and Cisco Secure Email Gateway CVE-2026-76519.
topics.summary: All three products sit at the edge of enterprise networks and hand an attacker command execution: Langflow runs AI workflows, the Collabora app renders documents inside Nextcloud, and AhsayCBS manages backups. Patch Langflow and AhsayCBS now, disable or update the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server app, and search web directories for files that execute commands.

sources.title: Langflow's Critical Authenticated RCE Flaw Targeted in 1,423 Honeypot Exploit Attempts

topics.title: Hirudo Swaps Indonesian Banking Apps for Patched Copies
topics.latest_developments: ThreatFabric, the Dutch mobile security company, disclosed a new Android banking trojan it calls Hirudo that uninstalls a victim's legitimate banking application and installs a repackaged copy with the app's own security checks switched off from the inside, and it carries ready-made replacements for eight Indonesian banking apps.
topics.summary: Hirudo combines a banking trojan with a full remote access trojan, so the operator both harvests credentials from the counterfeit app and drives the handset directly. Banks should treat app integrity and reinstallation events as fraud signals, and Android users should install financial apps only from Google Play and refuse requests to sideload an update.

sources.title: Novel Android RAT 'Hirudo' Replaces Banking Apps With Trojanized Copies
Hirudo Android Trojan Uses Patched Banking Apps to Bypass Their Built-In Security Checks

topics.title: Spyware Infects Phones Through Ad Networks
topics.latest_developments: Wired reported on October 15, 2026 that researchers at The Citizen Lab released the first technical evidence of sophisticated mercenary spyware traveling through online advertising, infecting phones with no click from the owner, and The Record reported that Prime Minister Donald Tusk, who ordered Poland's investigation into the surveillance operation the previous ruling party ran, said the spyware manufacturer itself held access to the data Polish operators harvested and called the affair one of the biggest scandals in Polish history since the fall of communism.
topics.summary: Mercenary spyware vendors sell phone-compromise services to government customers, and targeted advertising gives them a delivery channel that reaches a chosen handset without a message or a link. Executives, journalists, and government personnel who face this threat should keep phones on current operating system versions, enable lockdown modes where the vendor offers them, and treat ad-blocking at the network edge as a security control.

sources.title: 'Nightmare Scenario': Zero-Click Spyware Is Infecting Phones via Targeted Ads
Spyware manufacturer had access to data harvested by former Polish government, current PM says

topics.title: CenterPoint Energy and the Legal Aid Agency Count Their Losses
topics.latest_developments: CenterPoint Energy began telling roughly 1 million Texans that a breach exposed their names, addresses, Social Security numbers, and driver's license numbers, and the Legal Aid Agency, the executive agency of the United Kingdom's Ministry of Justice that runs the Public Defender Service, said the attackers who broke into its IT systems in April 2025 took records reaching back to 1978.
topics.summary: CenterPoint Energy distributes electricity and natural gas across Texas and holds the identity documents utilities collect to open an account, the combination that fuels identity theft. The Legal Aid Agency holds financial and criminal case details on people who applied for legal aid over nearly five decades, and anyone who applied since 1978 should assume exposure and watch credit files and benefit accounts.

sources.title: CenterPoint Energy Data Breach Impacts 1 Million Texans
UK Legal Aid Agency: Hackers stole records dating back to 1978

topics.title: GhostAction Drains Secrets From 30,000 Repositories
topics.latest_developments: GitGuardian measured a sharp escalation of the GhostAction credential-theft campaign on October 8 and 9, 2026: the operators compromised the GitHub accounts of about 1,900 users, reached more than 30,000 repositories belonging to 3,000 users and organizations, and tried to pull 3,174 secrets out of the continuous integration configurations of public repositories.
topics.summary: GhostAction steals a maintainer's GitHub credentials, then pushes a workflow that exports every token, key, and password the repository's automation holds, which carries the attacker into cloud accounts and package registries downstream. Development teams should rotate CI secrets, require phishing-resistant multifactor authentication on GitHub accounts, and review recent workflow file changes.

sources.title: GhostAction Compromises About 1,900 GitHub Accounts, Targets Over 30,000 Repositories

topics.title: Cryptomus Sanctioned as Police Take OLVX
topics.latest_developments: The United Kingdom imposed economic sanctions on Cryptomus, the cryptocurrency platform experts call a major conduit for ransomware, narcotics, darknet market, and fraud payments and a channel that helps Russia work around existing financial restrictions; North Macedonia's Interior Ministry, working with the FBI, raided a home in a North Macedonian village and arrested the suspected administrator of the OLVX cybercrime market; and the Brooklyn District Attorney's office took down the servers and domains behind a cryptocurrency fraud scheme that Russian-speaking residents of Brooklyn first reported to local authorities three years ago.
topics.summary: Cryptomus processes payments for cybercrime services, and sanctions bar British firms from transacting with it, which raises the cost of cashing out for ransomware crews and darknet vendors. OLVX sold stolen accounts and credentials; firms should check exposure lists and compliance screening against the newly designated entity.

sources.title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
North Macedonian police arrest alleged administrator behind OLVX cybercrime market
Brooklyn DA's office disrupts crypto scam targeting Russian community

topics.title: PEERSTITCH Implant Hides in FortiGate Firewalls
topics.latest_developments: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 published an intrusion investigation on October 14, 2026 in which attackers exploited CVE-2024-47575, the FortiManager authentication flaw, reached more than 500 managed firewalls, and deployed PEERSTITCH, memory-resident ARM64 malware that leaves nothing on the appliance's disk.
topics.summary: FortiManager centrally administers FortiGate firewalls, so one compromised manager carries an attacker to every device it controls, and a memory-resident implant survives no reboot yet also evades file-based scanning. Organizations running FortiManager should confirm they applied the CVE-2024-47575 fix Fortinet shipped in 2024, rotate device credentials, and compare running firewall configurations against known-good baselines.

sources.title: Unit 42 Uncovers PEERSTITCH, a Stealthy FortiGate Implant

business_politics.title: The AI Selloff Spreads Worldwide
business_politics.latest_developments: The rout that hit Wall Street on Wednesday widened Thursday, October 15: the Nikkei fell 2.9%, European and Asian chipmakers slid, Nasdaq futures dropped sharply, and 10-year Treasury and German Bund yields reached multiweek lows as investors retreated into government bonds.
business_politics.summary: Investors have begun doubting how long the artificial intelligence build-out can support equity valuations, with a failed initial public offering and slower-than-expected revenue growth at Anthropic feeding the doubt. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. reported record third-quarter earnings of $23.6 billion on AI demand the same morning and signaled willingness to expand in Texas, which shows the split between the chipmakers' order books and the market's mood.

business_politics.title: Zelenskyy Ends the Truce and Hits Refineries Again
business_politics.latest_developments: Volodymyr Zelenskyy told the Financial Times on Thursday, October 15, that Ukraine has resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries and called Washington's withdrawal of intelligence sharing and the weakening of Starlink service dangerous, and European leaders now plan to urge him to rein in his criticism of President Trump.
business_politics.summary: Limits on Kyiv's access to military-grade Starlink terminals set off panic among Ukrainian officials and several United States lawmakers and marked Trump's turn against Zelenskyy, weeks after the president announced an energy ceasefire that Moscow never honored. European capitals fear the public fight between the two leaders costs Ukraine American weapons and intelligence while Russian refining capacity again becomes a target.

business_politics.title: PNC Falls Short on Revenue
business_politics.latest_developments: PNC Financial Services Group reported Thursday, October 15, that third-quarter revenue rose and still missed Wall Street estimates, with $36 million of integration costs from its FirstBank acquisition denting profit, while Bank of New York Mellon posted net income applicable to shareholders of $1.61 billion, or $2.34 a share, up from $1.34 billion a year earlier.
business_politics.summary: PNC, headquartered in downtown Pittsburgh, is building a national retail and commercial franchise through acquisitions, and the integration bill now shows up in its quarterly numbers. The report lands as the Wall Street Journal finds rising interest rates and weak bond markets threatening the trading revenue that carried JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, and Citigroup through the quarter.

business.title: Homer City Plant's Water Permit Draws Objections
business.latest_developments: Indiana County residents asked Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection officials on Wednesday, October 14, to reject or rewrite a wastewater permit amendment that would let the proposed Homer City Generation power plant discharge as much as 6.8 million gallons of hot, polluted water a day into an Indiana County creek.
business.summary: Homer City Generation wants the amendment for the power plant planned at the site of the retired Homer City coal-fired station, roughly 50 miles east of Pittsburgh. The residents who spoke told the state the heated discharge will kill aquatic life in the creek, and the department has yet to rule on the request.

business.summary: Dick's Sporting Goods, which runs its company from Coraopolis in Allegheny County, uses the discount format to clear inventory at lower prices. The Hempfield conversion keeps the Westmoreland County storefront occupied by the same retailer.

around_town.title: Route 228 Widening Wins $102 Million
around_town.latest_developments: WPXI reported Wednesday evening, October 14, that $102 million has been approved for the Route 228 widening in Butler County, a project decades in the making, and that Pennsylvania Department of Transportation officials say one stretch of road remains to widen.
around_town.summary: Route 228 carries commuters across southern Butler County through Cranberry Township and Mars toward the Interstate 79 and Pennsylvania Turnpike interchanges, and PennDOT has widened the corridor in segments for years as housing and warehouses filled in around it.

around_town.latest_developments: KDKA's Ricky Sayer reported Wednesday night, October 14, that Washington Township in Fayette County has put its plan to take over the township municipal authority on pause after residents packed a meeting and demanded answers.
around_town.summary: The proposal would move the Washington Township Municipal Authority's operations under the township government. Residents at Wednesday's meeting pressed township leaders on how the transfer would work before the plan advances.
